name: Satish Dhanasekaran
current_role: President and CEO, Keysight Technologies; director, Zebra Technologies
profile: Engineer-turned-executive who joined Agilent (Keysight's predecessor) in 2006 and rose through its communications business to COO before becoming Keysight's second-ever CEO on May 1, 2022. Wealth is from executive equity rather than founding. He now runs the ~$5B test-and-measurement company spanning 5G/6G, AI data-center interconnect, quantum and aerospace/defense.
interesting_fact: Before becoming CEO he led Keysight's multi-billion-dollar Communications Solutions Group and is credited with helping establish Keysight's leadership in 5G test; he also sponsors Keysight's seat on the FCC Technological Advisory Committee and the NextG Alliance.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a master's in electrical engineering from Florida State University and started at the company in 2006 as an engineer before moving into management.
notes: Hired executive, not a founder. Keysight's AI data-center interconnect (1.6T) test work is a natural podcast hook. Route via Keysight corporate communications (Andrea Mueller listed as worldwide editorial contact).

name: John M. Foraker
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and Chair, Once Upon a Farm, PBC (NYSE: OFRM)
profile: Packaged-food operator who spent 11 years as CEO of Annie's, taking it public in 2012 and selling it to General Mills in 2014, then ran the Annie's unit inside General Mills until 2017. He then co-founded organic kids' food brand Once Upon a Farm (with actress Jennifer Garner as co-founder/chief brand officer), which he now runs as a newly public benefit corporation.
interesting_fact: He has now led two natural-food brands to the public markets: Annie's (IPO 2012, sold to General Mills 2014) and Once Upon a Farm, which listed as OFRM; Jennifer Garner is his co-founder.
deep_cut_fact: Before food, he was a Bank of America vice president managing commercial banking relationships in its premium wine portfolio; he studied agricultural economics at UC Davis before a Berkeley MBA.
notes: Consumer-food founder rather than energy/data-center; good for an entrepreneurship/serial-operator angle. Media route is ICR. Some sources differ on exact Annie's CEO dates.

name: John E Williams Jr
current_role: Founding partner, Williams Hart & Boundas LLP (formerly Williams Kherkher), Houston; independent director, Stellar Bancorp; Houston Astros board
profile: John Eddie Williams Jr. is a Houston trial lawyer who founded his firm in 1983 and made his fortune in mass torts, most famously as one of five private lawyers on Texas's 1990s tobacco litigation 'Dream Team' that recovered ~$17.3B. He still leads mass-tort cases and sits on the boards of Stellar Bancorp (via the CBTX merger), the Houston Astros and the Houston Police Foundation.
interesting_fact: Baylor's football field at McLane Stadium is named John Eddie Williams Field after his gift; he graduated first in his class at Baylor Law in 1978.
deep_cut_fact: He was in coach Grant Teaff's first signing class at Baylor, first took the field in August 1972, and is still part of the 'Stud Ducks' club of old Baylor teammates; he is the son and grandson of longshoremen and credits Teaff's goal-setting for his law-school success.
notes: SEC filer 'John E Williams Jr' (Stellar Bancorp director) matches John Eddie Williams Jr. per MarketScreener (lists Williams Kherkher). Lawyer/banker, weak fit for energy/data-center theme. Best route is via his law firm.

name: Seth P Bernstein
current_role: President and CEO, AllianceBernstein; Senior EVP and Head of Asset Management, Equitable Holdings
profile: Career asset-management executive who spent 32 years at JPMorgan (CFO of its Investment Management & Private Banking unit, then a decade as global head of Fixed Income & Currency) before becoming AllianceBernstein CEO in 2017. He led AB's high-profile 2018 headquarters relocation from New York to Nashville and runs the ~$900B+ AUM manager, majority-owned by Equitable.
interesting_fact: He moved AllianceBernstein's global HQ and ~1,050 jobs from Manhattan to Nashville, saying Nashville was the 'clear winner by every metric we analyzed' after a 30-city search; the HQ opened in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a BA in political science and economics from Haverford College, and before running JPMorgan's fixed income business he was CFO of JPMorgan's Investment Management & Private Banking division.
notes: Hired executive, not founder. AB has published on AI/data-center power investment themes, a possible hook. Route via AB media relations.

name: Nicola Loporcaro
current_role: Chairman and CEO, GMR Solutions Inc. (Global Medical Response, NYSE: GMRS)
profile: Nicola 'Nick' Loporcaro is a healthcare executive who spent nearly two decades at McKesson (president of McKesson Canada, later head of U.S. Pharma and Specialty Health), then ran Landmark Health until its 2021 sale to UnitedHealth/Optum. He became CEO of KKR-backed Global Medical Response, the largest U.S. ambulance/air-medical provider, in 2023 and took it public on the NYSE in May 2026.
interesting_fact: He led Global Medical Response (AMR ambulances, air-medical services) through its May 2026 NYSE IPO under the ticker GMRS, with KKR remaining the controlling shareholder.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a mechanical engineer at McGill University in Montreal, and also chairs the board of the nonprofit United States of Care.
notes: Goes by Nick Loporcaro. Hired operator (KKR portfolio CEO), not founder. Emergency medical services rather than energy; route via GMR PR (Kirsten Gurmendi, media@gmr.net).

name: Diedre J Gray
current_role: EVP, General Counsel, Chief Administrative Officer and Corporate Secretary, Post Holdings
profile: St. Louis corporate lawyer who joined Post Holdings at its 2011 spin-off from Ralcorp and rose to EVP, General Counsel and Chief Administrative Officer, overseeing legal and administrative functions through Post's long run of food-brand acquisitions. Earlier she practiced securities and M&A law at Bryan Cave and was associate GC at MEMC Electronic Materials (later SunEdison). Wealth stems from executive equity.
interesting_fact: Before Post she was associate general counsel at MEMC Electronic Materials, the solar-wafer maker that became SunEdison, giving her an early link to the solar/energy industry.
deep_cut_fact: At the University of Missouri she was chief of staff of the Missouri Students Association; she now serves as vice president of the board of St. Louis's Center of Creative Arts (COCA) and on the board of Forest Park Forever.
notes: In-house executive (general counsel), low public profile and not a natural podcast guest; route via Post media relations. The MEMC/SunEdison stint is the only energy tie.

name: Enrique Lores
current_role: President and CEO, PayPal Holdings (since March 1, 2026); formerly President and CEO of HP Inc. (2019-2026)
profile: Spanish-born engineer who joined HP as a summer intern in 1989 and spent ~36 years there, leading the 2015 Hewlett-Packard/HPE separation and serving as HP Inc. CEO from November 2019. A PayPal director since ~2021 and its board chair from July 2024, he was named PayPal CEO in February 2026, succeeding Alex Chriss. Wealth is from executive equity.
interesting_fact: He went from HP intern to HP CEO over 30 years, then jumped from PayPal's board chair seat into its CEO job in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He only stayed at HP because, after his 1989 summer internship in the U.S., HP was opening a center in Spain and offered him a job; he said he 'thought it would be cool to do for a couple of years' and later described running the HP/HPE split as 'like founding a company.'
notes: Input lists him as HP CEO; that is outdated - he left HP to become PayPal CEO effective March 1, 2026. Electrical engineering degree (UPV Valencia) and Esade MBA. Route via PayPal media relations.

name: G Patrick Lynch
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Northern Technologies International Corp. (NTIC); stepped down as President & CEO in September 2026
profile: Long-time leader of Minnesota-based NTIC, maker of ZERUST vapor-corrosion-inhibitor products, Zerust Oil & Gas solutions and Natur-Tec compostable bioplastics, sold largely through a global network of joint ventures. He joined NTIC in 1995, was President from 2005 and CEO from 2006, and in September 2026 handed the CEO role to Gautam Ramdas and became Chairman. He is an officer/director of Inter Alia Holding Co., a major NTIC holder.
interesting_fact: NTIC's ZERUST line traces to the company's 1973 vapor-capsule corrosion diffuser and what it calls the world's first VCI film (1979); the company operates via ~29 joint ventures worldwide and serves oil & gas infrastructure through Zerust Oil & Gas.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining NTIC he worked in sales management for Fuji Electric in Tokyo and in programming project management for BMW in Munich; he holds an MBA from Michigan's Ross School of Business.

public_contacts.value: Company contact listed as Matthew Wolsfeld, CFO, (763) 225-6600 (no email published)

notes: Input lists him as CEO; as of Sept 4, 2026 he is Chairman (Gautam Ramdas is CEO). Corrosion protection for oil & gas/energy infrastructure is a relevant angle. Only published company contact is the CFO's office phone line in press releases.

name: Dave Waiser
current_role: Founder of Gett (GetTaxi); current role not verified
profile: Dave (Shahar) Waiser is the Israeli entrepreneur who founded GetTaxi (later Gett) with Roi More, a ride-hailing and corporate ground-transport platform that reached a ~$1B+ valuation. Gett's Israeli and international business was sold to Pango (deal announced May 2024 for $175M) and Lyft agreed in April 2026 to buy Gett's UK operations for GBP 40M.
interesting_fact: Gett's UK operations are being folded into Lyft's European platform Freenow after Lyft agreed in April 2026 to buy them for GBP 40 million.
deep_cut_fact: The idea for GetTaxi came to him in summer 2009 while he waited about 30 minutes for a taxi to the airport in Palo Alto, California.
notes: Wikipedia's History section calls him Shahar Waiser; the infobox says Dave Waiser - same person. Web search budget ran out mid-lane, so his current venture and any published contact could not be verified; check his LinkedIn/X before outreach.

name: Martin Villig
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman of the Board, Bolt (Estonia)
profile: Estonian tech entrepreneur who co-founded ride-hailing/mobility company Bolt (originally Taxify, 2013) with his younger brother, CEO Markus Villig, after stints running Skype's web backend team and strategic projects at Fortumo. Bolt operates ride-hailing, scooters, car rental and delivery across Europe and Africa. He is a prominent Estonian philanthropist and startup-ecosystem builder.
interesting_fact: He has publicly pledged to give 50% of his annual income and eventually 90% of his wealth to charity, and co-founded the ~EUR 3M Heateo Education Fund with Wise co-founder Taavet Hinrikus.
deep_cut_fact: He won Estonia's first-ever Business Olympiad in 1997 as a schoolboy, led Skype's web backend (self-service and payments) team in 2005-2007, co-founded the Garage48 hackathon series, and in 2024 co-founded the Cool Padel center in Tallinn's Mustamae district.
notes: Estonian Wikipedia article is flagged for limited citations; verify details before quoting. Daily cyclist and urban-mobility advocate (board of Elav Tanav). Route via Bolt press office.

name: Monish Darda
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Mentor (board member), Icertis
profile: Pune/Seattle-based enterprise-software entrepreneur who co-founded contract-lifecycle-management company Icertis with Samir Bodas in 2009 after launching BladeLogic's India R&D operation (BladeLogic was acquired by BMC). As long-time CTO he built the Icertis Contract Intelligence platform used by Airbus, Daimler, J&J, Microsoft and Sanofi; he now serves as Co-founder & Chief Mentor while Jim Moffatt and Rajat Bahri are co-CEOs.
interesting_fact: He led Icertis's AI and blockchain work, which landed the company on Forbes' AI 50 list two years running, and he is co-inventor on two patents in cloud resource management and provisioning.
deep_cut_fact: He is an avid PlayStation 4 gamer (especially Call of Duty: Warzone), a Formula 1 fan and an Isaac Asimov science-fiction reader; he trained as a mechanical engineer and earned a master's from Florida Atlantic University.
notes: No longer CTO/operational lead; title is Chief Mentor. LinkedIn is linked from his official company bio. Wikipedia's Icertis article is outdated (lists Bodas as CEO).
